signed_payload:
[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Type: Time (Minutes)
- Amount: 180
- Description: KAN-102: terminal-goal sessions no longer false-nag (partial vs ticket spec) + #675 CI guard fix
  
  Pull requests (GitHub evidence):
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/673
  - https://github.com/TrueSightDAO/truesight_autopilot/pull/675
  
  Details:
  Work on truesight_autopilot loop-hygiene, 2026-11-27/28. Two PRs merged, deployed and verified live. KAN-102 closed Done, with an honest scope caveat noted at the end.
  
  === #675 — merge guard conflated "CI still running" with "CI failed" ===
  Every refusal for three turns ended with "Failing/pending checks: (unnamed)". Three distinct conditions were being collapsed into one message:
  - unstable = checks still running -> should mean wait and retry
  - red = checks genuinely failed -> should mean stop and fix
  - (unnamed) = the gh PAT gets 403 on the Checks API -> means "I cannot see", not "it failed"
  
  Proven empirically on #668, which merged clean on retry with zero code change. The word "Failing" sent the operator hunting defects that did not exist. A guardrail that fails closed for the wrong reason trains the operator to ignore it — worse than no guardrail.
  
  === #673 — KAN-102: terminal goal must not classify as awaiting a decision ===
  Root cause took three attempts; the two wrong ones are the useful part:
  
  1. "Stop marking every message awaiting" — WRONG. The registry is a reaction go-signal map; any emoji on any message means continue. Selective marking would have broken emoji-go.
  2. "Suppress the prompt if the session acted after it" — WRONG, killed by timestamps: goal complete at 22:17:35, but the closing report re-marked awaiting at 22:17:41. The prompt is NEWER than completion, so every time-based rule concludes "governor has not acted" and leaves the nag firing. The closing report re-armed the trap on the way out.
  3. ACTUAL invariant: a session whose goal reached a terminal state has no open work left to decide about, so no resume-awaiting entry can be a live question. Semantic, not temporal.
  
  Change: classify_session gains goal_status; both AWAITING and AWAITING_STALE gated on "not goal_terminal"; TERMINAL_GOAL_STATES = {completed, dismissed}; loop_daemon.load_goal_states() returns session -> status for every goal. Deliberately asymmetric — goal_status=None behaves exactly as before, so a goalless or OPEN-goal session can still raise a genuine question. A guard that silenced real questions would be worse than the nag.
  
  === REBASE HAZARD (caught) ===
  main's #613 added load_goal_ages() in the same file, sharing a "return out" trailer with the new load_goal_states(). The first conflict resolution concatenated both sides and dropped it — 14 test failures. Shipping that would have silently disabled #613's staleness feature. Caught only by running the suite after rebasing rather than trusting a clean-looking rebase.
  
  === GATES (pinned ruff 0.15.16, matching CI) ===
  compileall rc=0; ruff check app tests scripts All checks passed; format advisory on my 3 files; scripts/smoke_tools.py rc=0 (83 schemas, 67 routes); pytest 2729 passed, 0 failed. Plus 5 new regression tests pinning both directions.
  
  Note: the box runs ruff 0.16.8 while CI pins 0.15.16, which produced 798 phantom errors — my local "green" had been measuring a different linter than CI. Isolated venv used for a true reading. scripts/preflight.py (#677) now automates CI-exact parity, so this is fixed at the tooling level.
  
  === DEPLOY + LIVE VERIFY ===
  deploy_autopilot returned noop/already on c50cc7f. Not taken at face value: code on disk confirmed at c50cc7f on main; daemon process start 08:46:05 vs code mtime 01:28:25 (booted after new code landed); all three services active.
  Live reconcile(): terminal-goal sessions wrongly awaiting = 0.
  The single remaining awaiting_stale is a session with goal status "open" ("Work through all 6 Jira tickets...") — correctly NOT suppressed, which is the intended asymmetry.
  
  === HONEST SCOPE CAVEAT ===
  KAN-102's FIX section specified decision-TAGGING at the load_awaiting() boundary (tag only explicit resume_awaiting=True or options[] messages; clear entries on complete/dismiss). What actually shipped is goal-terminality gating at the classifier. Verified by inspection: load_awaiting() still passes ALL registry entries, and no clear-on-complete exists.
  
  Consequence: the reported defect is fixed (a completed goal can no longer nag), but a plain status report in a session with an OPEN goal could still surface as a decision prompt — visible live as the one remaining awaiting_stale. The ticket's four acceptance tests are therefore NOT all met by #673. The residual is a distinct design change and is being proposed as follow-up work rather than claimed as done.
  
  No ledger writes. No production deploys beyond the autopilot box. Irreversible actions: none.
- Contributor(s): Sophia Truesight
- TDG Issued: 300.00
- Attached Filename: N/A
- Destination Contribution File Location: N/A
